draft.title: Belief systems and power
card: Belief systems and ideologies can shape who holds power and how people respond to it. They can work in more than one direction.
Those in power may use a belief system or ideology to explain why their rule is right. When people accept this reasoning, it can help keep the rulers in place.
People may also use a belief system or ideology to question those in power. It can give them shared values to argue for change, and a way to organise others.
The same belief system can be used on both sides. What matters is how people use it in a given time and place, not the belief system alone.
draft.remember: A belief system or ideology can be used to back those in power or to challenge them.

a.q: Which example shows a belief system being used to challenge those in power?
opts: Church members cite their faith to protest an unjust law
A king says his rule is approved by the gods
A government teaches a national ideology in all schools
Leaders quote scripture to justify their right to rule
a.why: The church members use their faith to question a law and argue for change. The other options use beliefs to justify or protect those already in power, so they show support, not challenge.
a.clue: Look for the group using beliefs to argue against authority.

b.q: In one country, rulers cite a religion to defend their authority. In the same country, a reform group cites the same religion to demand fairer laws. What does this show?
opts: One belief system can be used to support or challenge power
The reform group has misunderstood the religion
A religion can only support those who hold power
Rulers and reformers must belong to different religions
b.why: Both sides draw on the same belief system, but for opposite purposes. This shows how people use a belief system matters. It is wrong to say a religion can only support power, because the reform group is using it to challenge power.
b.clue: Both groups use the same belief system for different aims.

a.best: Church members cite their faith to protest an unjust law

b.best: One belief system can be used to support or challenge power

problems.detail: Two distractors use absolutes ('must belong', 'can only support') that students learn to reject on sight. The right option is the only hedged one and nearly repeats the remember line, so it stands out without understanding the idea.

check.summary: The card, remember line and question a are accurate and stay within the point. In question b, the absolute wording in two distractors and the right option's echo of the remember line make the answer easy to spot without knowing the idea.

b.q: In one country, rulers cite a religion to defend their authority. In the same country, a reform group cites the same religion to demand fairer laws. What does this show?
opts: What matters is how each group uses the religion
What matters is which side the religion itself favours
The reform group's reading of the religion is less valid
Religious beliefs tend to discourage calls for change
